[DIN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978) establishes candidate-conditioned history weighting through a local activation network; candidate matching alone is established prior art. [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) models positions and time intervals, but temporal attention does not guarantee monotonic recency preference. A reproducible proposed recency bias is a_t(j)=softmax_t[m(e_j,h_t)−λ log(1+Δ_t)], λ≥0, with Δ explicitly defined as positional lag or elapsed time. Mask padding and all positions beyond the prediction prefix; contextual history representations must also be causal.

[Item-item collaborative filtering](https://archives.iw3c2.org/www10/cdrom/papers/519/index.html) supplies the neighborhood-aggregation foundation. For an explicit sparse implementation, define binary training-only user-item incidence X, C=XᵀX, d_i=C_ii, and zero the diagonal. Compare raw C_ij, cosine C_ij/√(d_i d_j), and lift N·C_ij/(d_i d_j). Cosine moderates frequency effects without eliminating popularity; lift corrects against independent popularity but can amplify rare coincidences. Apply minimum support, shrinkage C_ij/(C_ij+τ), and fixed top-K pruning. Proposed recurring-interest support R(j)=Σ_{t≤p}w_t S_{i_t,j} measures repeated neighborhood evidence; compare against max_t S_{i_t,j} and support from distinct history items. Co-occurrence alone does not establish temporal recurrence or periodicity. Prefix masking prevents sequence leakage; training-only graph construction prevents held-out-label leakage, while strict event-time causality additionally requires time-filtered graph counts.

Recommended controls: candidate matching only; matching+recency; matching+recurrence; all three; graph-only and popularity-only baselines. Compare normalized versus raw graphs and degree-preserving shuffled graphs; report validation HR@10 by popularity and history-length strata alongside the required macro average. Keep seeds, candidates, splits, tuning budgets and graph construction fixed. These are proposed controls, not reported experimental findings or evidence of novelty.
